hints: In either case the relative distance is the sum of the lengths. Only the relative speed changes.
worded:
1. To cross completely, the passenger train must move 60 + 120 = 180 m relative to the freight train, in both cases.

2. Same direction: relative speed 80 − 30 = 50 km/h. Opposite: 80 + 30 = 110 km/h.

3. Same distance, so time ∝ 1/speed: t₁/t₂ = 110/50 = 11/5. (C)
mistakes: The ratio is inverse to the relative speeds; don’t invert it to 5/11.
